ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is yellowish-brown with a distinct dark hourglass pattern on the dorsum and granular skin. It inhabits *Ochlandra* bamboo thickets.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes ochlandrae* is best distinguished by its unique, distinctively bright, translucent golden-yellow iris, which contrasts sharply with the eyes of similar species.
ai.habitat: The Ochlandrae Reed Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, specifically breeding within the hollow internodes of *Ochlandra* reed bamboo.
ai.behavior: The Ochlandrae Reed Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the stalks of bamboo plants in its native Western Ghats habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes ochlandrae* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females laying small clutches in bamboo.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ochlandrae Reed Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 100 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Raorchestes ochlandrae* produces a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call, typically heard from within dense reed beds in its swampy habitat.
